Water's getting colder. Here's the quick way to pick a wetsuit.

4/3 means 4 mm on your body and 3 mm on arms and legs. Thicker keeps you warm, thinner makes paddling easier.

Go one step warmer if it's windy, if you sit and wait a lot, or if you get cold easily. And if water flushes in, it's usually the size, not the thickness.

Getting pushed back to the beach every time the foam hits? You need a way under it, not over it.

Rule of thumb: board over 7 feet or a foamie, turtle roll. Grab the rails, flip under, let the foam pass, flip back and keep paddling.
Shorter hard board: duck dive. Push the nose down, knee or foot on the tail, follow the board under and come up behind the foam.

Start the move about 6 feet before the foam hits. And never let go of your board. A loose board can hit the surfer behind you.

2026-10-19.caption:
Two forecasts say 3 feet. One day is a mess, the other is perfect. The difference is the period.

Period is the seconds between two waves passing the same spot.
6 s: wind swell. Choppy, weak, close together.
12 s: ground swell. Clean lines with real push.

Beginner tip: long-period waves carry more power, even when they look small. On those days stay in the whitewater or pick a sheltered spot.

You pop up, you stand, and the board runs straight to the sand. Here's how to ride along the wave instead.

1. Look where you want to go, down the line. Not at your feet
2. Turn your shoulders and chest toward the open face. The board follows
3. Light pressure: toes when you face the wave, heels when your back is to it
4. Start the angle at the take-off. Paddle in with the nose pointed a little toward the open face

2026-10-22.caption:
First session and everyone is talking about sets, peaks and closeouts? Here's what they mean.

Set: a group of bigger waves that come in together.
Peak: the highest point of a wave, where it starts to break.
Whitewater: the foam after the wave breaks. Where you learn.
Closeout: breaks all at once along its length. Let it go.
Lineup: where surfers sit and wait, just past the break.
Drop in: taking a wave someone closer to the peak is already riding. Don't.
Duck dive: pushing a short board under an oncoming wave.
Leash: the cord from the tail to your back ankle.
Wax: grip on the deck. Pick it by water temperature.
Offshore: wind from land to sea, clean waves. Onshore: wind from the sea, choppy waves.

2026-10-23.caption:
You will fall. A lot. Here's how to do it without getting hurt.

1. Fall flat and to the side, like a starfish. Away from the board, never in front of it.
2. Never head first. The bottom is often closer than it looks, especially in the shallows.
3. Hold your breath, then relax. Fighting burns air. Most beginner hold-downs last only a few seconds.
4. Come up with your arms over your head. Your board may be right above you.

2026-10-24.caption:
A lot of beginners start on a board that's too small. Here's a simple way to size your first one.

Rule of thumb: about 1 liter of volume per kg of body weight. 155 lb (70 kg)? Look for 70 L or more.
Go bigger if your waves are soft or you're still building paddle fitness.
Soft-top first: a foam deck around 8 to 9 ft is stable and softer when you fall. Smaller build? 7 to 8 ft can work.
Too small too early means fewer waves caught and fewer pop-ups to practice.

2026-10-25.caption:
No waves this week? Ten minutes on the floor keeps you ready.

Warm up: 20 squats.
Then 3 rounds:
1. Pop-up drill × 10. Belly flat, push, land in your stance
2. Push-ups × 8. Knees down is fine
3. Back extension (superman) 30 s. Chest and arms up, like you're paddling
4. Plank 40 s. Elbows under shoulders
Rest 30 s between rounds.

It won't replace time in the water, but it helps your paddling strength and pop-up speed.

2026-10-26.caption:
Slipping off the deck or losing your board? It's usually the wax or the leash.

Wax
1. Two coats: a hard base coat first, then a softer top coat on it
2. Top coat by water temp: cold under 60°F (15°C), cool 58-68°F (14-20°C), warm 64-74°F (18-23°C), tropical 75°F+ (24°C+). Ranges vary a bit by brand
3. Crosshatch: diagonal lines one way, then across them
4. Longboard: wax the whole deck. Soft-top: little or none, the textured deck already grips

Leash
1. Same length as the board or a bit longer. 9' board, 9' leash or longer
2. On your back foot
3. Before each session, check the cord for nicks and the velcro for grip
